seo.title: Hawaii Summer Program | Pacific Discovery
seo.description: Hawaiʻi in 4 weeks: an Imu feast, Volcanoes National Park, manta rays, Mauna Kea stargazing, fishpond restoration, surf lessons and Hanauma Bay. Ages 17–22.

hero.headline: Surf, summit and service across two Hawaiian islands
hero.intro: Share an Imu feast in Pahala, snorkel with manta rays off Kona, stargaze from Mauna Kea, restore a fishpond in Hilo and learn to surf on Oʻahu.

itinerary.heading: Week by week
itinerary.note: This is a guide to what you can expect to do on program. The order in which activities occur might vary. Itineraries are subject to change.

weeks.title: Imu feast & Volcanoes National Park
weeks.body:
You’ll meet your Program Instructors in Hilo and head to Pahala in the district of Kaʻu for orientation. Over two days of Cultural Fest we prepare an imu, a traditional underground oven, then share the feast along with a musical group performance.

We explore Volcanoes National Park and its lava rock landscapes, then travel to the Kona side and set up camp at Hoʻokena. The week ends with a manta ray tour, heading out at night to snorkel or float as the mantas glide below.
weeks.imageAlt: Students hiking across rugged black lava rock near the coast

weeks.title: Farming service & Mauna Kea
weeks.body:
After a day exploring Kona we travel to Waimea and settle in at Waipiʻo Lodge. Two days on the Ulu Mau Puanui service project give us hands-on insight into traditional Hawaiian agriculture.

In Hilo we set up at Arnott’s and have an orientation session with Traven. Then we tour the summit of Mauna Kea to stargaze, learning about the night sky through high-powered telescopes, before a day to explore Hilo.

weeks.title: Fishpond restoration & surf on Oʻahu
weeks.body:
We spend two days on fishpond restoration in Hilo with the Edith Kanakaʻole Foundation, then fly to Oʻahu and settle into Haleʻiwa.

We snorkel at Shark Cove and spend two days on surf lessons with experienced instructors, learning paddling, pop-ups and how to read the waves, with time to explore Haleʻiwa in between. The week ends with the move to the Sun Farm yurts in Honolulu.
weeks.imageAlt: Surfers riding and paddling for waves below green hills

weeks.title: Hanauma Bay, service & farewell
weeks.body:
We snorkel Hanauma Bay, inside a volcanic crater on Oʻahu’s southeast coast, and visit Lyon Arboretum and Mānoa Falls. After a morning helping at the Hawaiʻi Food Bank, we hike an old railway track up the rim of Koko Crater for sunset.

A day of conservation work with Papahana is followed by an evening at Museum After Dark, and we kayak to the Twin Islands. We finish with our program wrap before flying home from Honolulu.

day.heading: What a typical day looks like

notes.title: Free time
notes.body: Each week there is some designated free time to catch up on email and laundry, rest and explore with others in the group.

notes.title: Phones & wifi
notes.body: We encourage flight mode so you stay present. Wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns.

notes.title: Fitness needed
notes.body: Medium activity level. Anyone with average fitness and enthusiasm for the outdoors will be fine. Expect hiking, surfing, snorkeling and kayaking, and some physical work on volunteer projects, like preparing beds for planting or removing invasive plants.

items.title: Certificate of Environmental Conservation
items.body: Earn a Certificate of Environmental Conservation for your 40 hours of service learning, from traditional farming with Ulu Mau Puanui to fishpond restoration in Hilo and conservation work with Papahana.

items.title: Optional college credit
items.body: Earn college credit through the University of Montana. 529 education funds can be used to pay for your credits and your Pacific Discovery program tuition.

faq.heading: Questions we get about this program

items.q: How fit do I need to be?
items.a: The program suits anyone of average fitness. Be ready for hiking, including a sunset hike up Koko Crater, plus surfing, snorkeling and kayaking. Volunteer projects also involve physical work, like preparing beds for planting or removing invasive plants.

items.q: Do I need to know how to surf?
items.a: No. Experienced instructors teach the fundamentals in Haleʻiwa: paddling, pop-ups and how to read the waves.

items.q: Do I get anything for the service hours?
items.a: Yes. You’ll earn a Certificate of Environmental Conservation for your 40 hours of service learning.
A mix of a cottage, a lodge and a hostel, camping at Hoʻokena and in Hilo, and yurts at Sun Farm in Honolulu.

Tuition covers all in-country transport, accommodation, meals, and the activities and entry fees in the itinerary. It doesn't cover flights to and from Hawaiʻi, travel insurance, spending money, optional college credit or optional activities.

items.q: How much spending money should I bring?
items.a: About $100 a week for snacks, laundry, personal shopping and optional activities. It varies from student to student.

items.q: Can I stay in touch with home?
items.a: Yes. We encourage keeping phones on flight mode so you stay present, and wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns. There will also be a photo album that students and instructors can upload photos and video to, so parents and caregivers can stay up to date.

safety.heading: For parents: how we keep students safe

items.title: 24/7 Emergency Line
items.body: Parents, students and instructors can reach a real person at any hour. Every call is logged and passed to our on-call staff member by phone.

items.title: Wilderness First Aid & Live Risk Assessment
items.body: All our instructors hold Wilderness First Aid (WFA) certification and have extensive training in group leadership and risk management.

items.title: Accredited Safety Systems
items.body: Our safety systems are assessed and accredited by the Gap Year Association (USA), Year Out Group (UK) and OutdoorsMark (NZ). Students on Go Overseas voted us one of the top gap year providers for safety.

items.title: Insurance & Health
items.body: Comprehensive travel insurance is required, covering medical costs and emergency evacuation. Check vaccinations with your doctor, and pack a first-aid kit and any personal medication. Our instructors can't legally give students any medication.
